studies.title: The map that named America
studies.caption: Martin Waldseemüller and Matthias Ringmann print a twelve-sheet map of the world that shows the lands across the Atlantic as a separate continent and names it America, after Amerigo Vespucci.
studies.prompt: Wide printer's workshop view at Saint-Die in1507: the large wall map assembled as TWELVE rectangular sheets in FOUR columns and THREE rows, inspected by a small standing printer at side. Broad modified Ptolemaic curved world outline, narrow separate Americas on left, Europe/Africa nearer centre, Asia right; geographic forms approximate period woodcut, not modern map. Paper seams and printing work are focus. No readable labels or quotation, no Australia or satellite-accurate coasts.
